title: Add playhouse.archive for moving old rows to an archive table
description: Adds `playhouse/archive.py` with an `Archive` helper for tables that grow without bound (orders, events, logs). `Archive(Model).archive(where)` moves every row matching `where` into an archive table with the same columns and returns how many rows it moved; `restore(ids)` moves archived rows back by primary key. The archive table is named after the model's table with an `_archive` suffix unless `table_name` is given, and any name the database accepts works. Rows move in batches of `batch_size`, and each batch is copied and deleted in one transaction, so a row is never in both tables or in neither, even when a statement fails. `dry_run=True` only counts the rows that would move and leaves the database exactly as it was. A restored row whose primary key has been reused in the model's table in the meantime stays in the archive. Includes tests in `tests/archive.py`.

defects.summary: archive(dry_run=True) creates the archive table before it returns the count, so a dry run changes the database.
Each batch is selected with an offset of the rows already moved, but moved rows are deleted, so later batches skip rows and they are never archived.
The default archive table name is built from the model's class name instead of its table name, so a model with a custom table_name gets a wrongly named archive.

ceiling.summary: count() creates the archive table when it does not exist instead of returning 0, so reading the count changes the database, even right after a dry run or against a read-only connection.
